narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which
narrator.languages: master narration in English; translations per language in episodes/i18n/<lang>/<slug>.json with the same scene structure (pipeline/translate.py); names, places and counts are never translated

This is Rebolation. Early 21st century.

Title card: Rebolation · Brazil · Early 21st century

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Rebolation emerged in Brazilian rave parties in the early 2000s.
It was originally called 'reboleixon'.
In 2009, the name 'Free Step' was adopted by the community to distance the dance from the Axé music song 'Rebolation' by Parangolé.
on_screen: Map: Brazil · South America
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Originally a rave-based dance, it serves as a physical expression of electronic music.
It is a social, performative style that gained global visibility through internet video sharing.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The main move involves 'walking' by putting a foot forward and using the heel as a pivot point to turn the back foot backwards.
The front foot turns inwards around the heel.
Loose hand movements accompany the steps.
Watch for Heel-pivot walk.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (WGQAGTmc8Qs)
Captions name each signature move as it appears

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The dance is performed to electronic music, specifically psy trance and electro house.
The music provides the high-energy pulse required for the rapid footwork.
Listen for the Electronic synthesizers, Drum machines.
The music is characterized by the high-energy pulse of psy trance and electro house, providing a steady, driving beat for the dancer.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Traditional attire includes bell-bottomed 'shuffle pants' or phat pants with neon details, UV reflective tape, or glitter.
Modern practitioners often wear casual street clothing with flat-soled sneakers to aid in sliding.

narration: Ralph Morente (uploader of a popular 2008 YouTube video).
The dance is compared to the Melbourne Shuffle and Hardstyle.
The dance is considered a Brazilian version of the Melbourne Shuffle and Hardstyle.

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Rebolation is influence of Melbourne Shuffle: Considered by many dancers as the Brazilian version of this style.
Rebolation is influence of Hardstyle: Considered by many dancers as the Brazilian version of this style.
Rebolation is sibling of Stepping: A similar style from Johannesburg, South Africa, originating around 2006.

steps_as_taught.name: Primeiro passo
steps_as_taught.description: Base movement involving shifting body weight to the front of the foot and moving legs forward and back.

steps_as_taught.name: Segundo passo
steps_as_taught.description: Similar to the first step, but throwing the leg backward instead of forward.

steps_as_taught.name: Terceiro passo
steps_as_taught.description: Similar to previous steps, but performed laterally to the side.

steps_as_taught.name: Quarto passo
steps_as_taught.description: Constantly opening and closing the heels while transferring weight between legs.
